one_liner: Senior VA contracting officer-level specialist who writes, negotiates and administers $30M–$100M architect-engineer and construction contracts for veterans' facilities under the FAR and VAAR.
fit_summary: This GS-14 role requires an active FAC-C (Professional), 4+ years of contracting experience including a year of GS-13-equivalent A-E/construction contract negotiation, and a bachelor's degree with 24 business-related semester hours. Nothing on file shows Daniel holds the FAC-C or has led federal construction contract actions, so Daniel would be screened out at the selective placement factor unless that certification and experience exist.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and federal transition candidates; status is not required.
Selective Placement Factor: active FAC-C (Professional) at the time of application, or you are found ineligible.

GS-1102 requirements: 4 years of contracting or related experience plus a 4-year degree with at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, economics, management or related fields (transcript required).

One year of specialized experience at the GS-13 level leading A-E and construction contract negotiations and applying FAR/VAAR, pricing arrangements and procurement law; no education substitution at GS-14.
Financial disclosure report, background investigation, online assessment and a 1-year probationary period.
strategy: Before investing time, confirm whether you hold an active FAC-C (Professional); if not, skip this posting because it is a hard screen-out.

If you lack the certification, aim for entry or developmental 1102 roles (GS-7/9 Contract Specialist, VA or DHS acquisition intern programs) or contracting-adjacent roles in emergency management grants and program analysis.

If IEM work involved supporting government procurements, proposals, FEMA Public Assistance cost documentation or contractor oversight, record it in your notes with dates, hours per week and dollar values; it may count as 'related' experience for lower grades.
For any 1102 application, keep the resume to two pages and mirror the posting's terms (FAR, RFP, source selection, small business) only where you genuinely did that work.
Apply early: applicants are referred in the order received, and the window is only October 30 to November 5, 2026.
Have your transcript showing the 24 business-related semester hours ready, since 1102 roles at every grade require it.
resume_bullets: Supported [government client] procurement for [type of emergency management/recovery services] valued at [$ amount], preparing [RFP sections, cost estimates, or evaluation documentation] in compliance with [FAR/applicable rules] ([dates], [hours/week]).

Reviewed [number] contractor invoices and cost documentation totaling [$ amount] for [disaster recovery program], verifying [funding eligibility/allowability] and flagging [issues] for [client/agency].
Served as primary liaison between [client agency] and [contractors/stakeholders] on [project], coordinating [meetings, deliverables, schedules] across [number] parties.
interview_questions: Walk us through how you planned and led negotiations on a complex architect-engineer or construction contract.
When would you choose an FPIF or CPIF arrangement over firm-fixed-price, and how would you justify it?
Describe a time you resolved a contracting issue not clearly addressed by the FAR or agency guidance.
How do you advise a program customer who wants a requirement that conflicts with small business or competition rules?
watch_outs: Active FAC-C (Professional) is required at application; without it you are automatically ineligible.
Seven-day window (closes November 5, 2026) with referral in order received, so late applicants may never be reviewed.
Not remote: ad hoc telework only, location set by vacancy, with recurring construction site inspections and a financial disclosure requirement.
GS-14 assumes years of senior contracting experience; your policy and people skills alone will not meet the specialized experience.
